title: Northern Vietnam
subtitle: Christmas to New Year · 9 days · 2 travellers

flights.carriers: Scoot · VietJet · Vietnam Airlines · Singapore Airlines
flights.fare: S$450–700 return per person — peak week, book 1–2 weeks out

expenses: ≈ S$883 per person on the ground (S$1,500 cap, flights excluded)

intro_beats.text: Changi to Noi Bai, non-stop, three hours twenty. Scoot, VietJet, Vietnam Airlines or Singapore Airlines all fly it, and Singapore passports enter visa-free for thirty days. Return fares in this week run four hundred and fifty to seven hundred Singapore dollars, and nothing is booked yet — lock the flights first. Here is the trip they hang off.

outro.heading: The budget
outro.text: Nine days, eight nights, about eight hundred and eighty Singapore dollars per person on the ground, inside a fifteen hundred cap that excludes flights. Book the flights first, then the bike and the permit, then the holiday hotels. Log what you spend as you go — these daily figures are the plan, not the bill.

days.title: Arrival + the Old Quarter on foot
days.caveat: Flights NOT YET BOOKED — S$450–700 return

beats.text: Day one. Changi to Noi Bai, then straight into the Old Quarter on foot — Hoan Kiem first, the lake the city is built around, and the red bridge to the temple island.
beats.caption: Hoàn Kiếm Lake

beats.text: St Joseph's Cathedral at dusk: neo-Gothic, peeling, and the streets around it are where the coffee and the crowds are.
beats.caption: St Joseph's Cathedral

beats.text: Then Dong Xuan market and a plastic stool — first pho, a cold beer, an early night. Nothing else is planned on purpose: the jet lag is real.
beats.caption: Đồng Xuân Market

days.title: Christmas Day in the Old Quarter: Temple of Literature, egg coffee, Long Biên Bridge at sunset

beats.text: Christmas Day starts at the Temple of Literature, Vietnam's first university, a thousand years old and quiet if you are there at opening.
beats.caption: Temple of Literature

beats.text: Hoa Lo Prison in the afternoon — the Hanoi Hilton — with a street-food walk for lunch in between, and egg coffee somewhere on the way.
beats.caption: Hỏa Lò Prison

beats.text: Long Bien Bridge at golden hour for the classic photograph, then pack a small bag and take the sleeper bus north at nine.
beats.caption: Long Biên Bridge

days.title: Loop day 1: Ha Giang → Quản Bạ 'Heaven's Gate' → Thẩm Mã pass → Yên Minh
days.caveat: Self-ride: SG licence + IDP not valid in VN

beats.text: Day three is the transfer: two hundred and ninety kilometres north out of the delta, four hours by limousine van, and the mountains start before Ha Giang.
In Ha Giang city you collect the bike — a 125cc semi-automatic, brakes, tyres, lights and helmet all checked before you pay — then ride up to Quan Ba's Heaven's Gate.
beats.caption: Quản Bạ 'Heaven's Gate'

beats.text: Confirm the border permit and the rental paperwork before you ride: the checkpoints are real, and a Singapore licence with an IDP is not valid here — unlicensed means uninsured.

days.title: Loop day 2
days.transit_note: Đồng Văn → Mèo Vạc · 22 km over Mã Pì Lèng

beats.text: Dong Van on a Sunday: the market, the H'mong King's Palace, and the stone houses of the old town.
Then Ma Pi Leng pass — twenty kilometres cut into the cliff above the Nho Que river, and the best road in the country.
beats.caption: Mã Pì Lèng Pass

beats.text: Take the boat through the gorge if the water is up, then sleep in Meo Vac with the pass behind you.
beats.caption: Nho Quế river

days.title: Loop day 3: Mèo Vạc → Dữ Già → back to Ha Giang city

beats.text: Loop day three: back through Du Gia and its waterfalls, the long way down to Ha Giang city.
beats.caption: Mèo Vạc

beats.text: Hot shower, laundry, thang co for dinner, and hand the bike back with the tank filled.
Sleep early. The van leaves at half past seven and the next day is all road.

days.title: Transit day: Ha Giang → Hanoi → Tam Coc

beats.text: Transit day, and the least glamorous one: Ha Giang down to Hanoi, then change vans.
South again to Tam Coc — the karst starts at the window before you arrive.
beats.caption: Ninh Bình

beats.text: Sunset over the paddies from the homestay roof, mountain goat for dinner. Book the vans a day ahead: the Hanoi change is what goes wrong.
beats.caption: Bái Đính

days.title: Hang Mua sunrise over Tam Coc

beats.text: Up before six for Hang Mua: five hundred stone steps to the dragon, and the best photograph of the trip looking down the river.
Then the long Trang An boat through the caves — two to three hours, and the short loop skips the best cave.
beats.caption: Tràng An

beats.text: Bicycles out to Bich Dong in the afternoon, golden hour over the rice on the way back.
beats.caption: Bái Đính Temple

days.title: Tam Coc boat at first light → Hanoi by late afternoon → NYE fireworks over Hoan Kiem Lake
bullets: Tam Coc boat at first light

beats.text: New Year's Eve. A quiet boat at first light in Tam Coc, then the road back to Hanoi.
Check in, eat early in the Old Quarter, and be at Hoan Kiem for midnight. The crowd is thick: pick a side and stay put.
beats.caption: Hoàn Kiếm, NYE

beats.text: Fireworks over the lake at midnight sharp, then walk back. Book the New Year hotel before October, because the Old Quarter fills.
beats.caption: Hanoi Opera House

beats.text: And out: Noi Bai, twenty-five kilometres, half an hour on a good morning — leave three hours before the flight.
beats.caption: Noi Bai (HAN)

beats.text: The first of January is a public holiday, so the airport is as busy as it gets. Keep the onward ticket on your phone, because the airline will ask.
